subject: Shiny server on Ubuntu 14.04: rmarkdown package was not found in the library

messages.author: 2065a7985d3de284
messages.subject: Shiny server on Ubuntu 14.04: rmarkdown package was not found in the library
parts:
On my newly installed Ubuntu 14.04, following official guide I've installed RStudio Server v0.98.978 and Shiny Server v1.2.0.359. Shiny is running fine and I can see "It's Alive" example at <myserver>:3838. But rmarkdown example fails with error like this: 

The application failed to start.
The application exited during initialization.
Error in eval(expr, envir, enclos): You are attempting to load an rmarkdown file, but the 
rmarkdown package was not found in the library. Ensure that 
rmarkdown is installed and is available in the Library of the 
user you're running this application as.
Calls: local -> eval.parent -> eval -> eval -> eval -> eval
Execution halted

It says I'm missing rmarkdown package. But I definitely installed it and it's working, for example I can run render function.

I tried to install rmarkdown packages both in R console and RStudio.
I've tried to read logs of shiny, no new information. 
I've tried to restart Shiny and even reinstall.
I didn't find solution in Administrator's Guide either.

Any ideas why rmarkdown example not works?

By the way, I've used this way to install rmarkdown package:
devtools::install_github("rstudio/rmarkdown")

messages.author: bbc57ffa8a14ad13
messages.subject: Re: Shiny server on Ubuntu 14.04: rmarkdown package was not found in the library
parts:
Hi Victor,

It's important to remember that shiny applications will (by default) run as the `shiny` user on the system. The only libraries that will be visible to the shiny user are ones that are installed globally in a system library or in the shiny user's personal library. The shell script command to install a package to the system library from CRAN is:

sudo su - -c "R -e \"install.packages('shiny', repos='http://cran.rstudio.com/')\""

You could modify this to install from GitHub using devtools using:

sudo su - -c "R -e \"library(devtools); install_github('rstudio/rmarkdown')\""

That should install not to your personal library, but to the global system library making rmarkdown visible to the shiny user in most systems.

Jeff
